findings.observation: There is a short vertical meteg stroke just left of the qamats under nun, seen in two overlapping slices. It has the same shape as the user-confirmed metegs in מְטַֽר and אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם. The candidate has no meteg here.

The marks read, right to left: sheva (ו), qamats (א) with a vertical stroke to its left, then patah (ס). The stroke sits between the qamats and the patah, so its host is alef, not samekh. In row04-part2 the same band shows a qof descender beside the etnahta of וּמַלְק֑וֹשׁ, which rules out a stray descender here. The candidate has no meteg.
There is a vertical stroke just left of the hiriq under tav, separate from the final-kaf descender next to the tipcha. No descending letter sits above it. The candidate has no meteg.
Same pattern as M1: a vertical stroke beside the qamats under nun, between the sheva (ו) and the patah (ת). The candidate has no meteg.
There is a vertical stroke beside the qamats under sin, between the bet sheva and the dalet sheva. It is separate from the final-kaf descender and tipcha further left. The candidate has no meteg.

The same patah, stroke, qamats, sheva sequence as M2 appears under ו-א-כ, with the stroke left of the alef qamats. The candidate has no meteg. The existing meteg on bet in וְשָׂבָֽעְתָּ matches the image, and the shin qamats there has no stroke.

A short vertical stroke appears between the vav patah and the ayin hataf patah. This is the same shape as the user-confirmed meteg in וַֽאֲבַדְתֶּ֣ם (row 7). But the vertical sheva dots of a hataf patah can merge into a stroke at this resolution, so I can't tell a meteg on ו from the hataf patah's own colon. The candidate has no meteg.

There is a vertical stroke next to a dot below the לא/יִ junction. It could be a meteg on lamed (לֹֽא־) or on the first yod beside its hiriq. Only one slice covers this word. The candidate has no meteg. The munach and segol under the second yod and the sheva under he are clear and correct.

There is an isolated dot above, between kaf and final mem. It sits lower than the row-0 shevas of תִּשְׁמְעוּ that show in the same band. It may be a speck or a mark carried over from row 0, but I can't tell from these slices, and only part2 covers the word. The candidate has no mark above it. The tipcha and segol under kaf are clear.

The zaqef qatan above tet falls in the band where row 6's segol and silluq under לָהֶֽם sit. I see vertical dots there, but I can't separate the zaqef from the row-6 marks. The zaqef on the mem of וְהָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה, on the same row, is clear.

scope_limitations: Scope is Deuteronomy 11:13–17, from וְהָיָ֗ה (block 3, word 0) through מֵעַל֙ (word 53), rows 0–7 only. This is not a review of the whole source page, the batch, the encoding or the export.

M1–M6 are all one kind of mark: a short vertical stroke next to a vowel (qamats, or hiriq in M3). Even at 3× these strokes are small, so each one should be confirmed by the user before it is applied. I did not use standard Bible pointing as evidence for or against them.
The overlapping slices don't line up exactly with the nominal 3× source_box coordinates. I matched marks between slices by the order of the glyphs, not by pixel position.

Divine Name holam: in rows 1 and 6 the holam dot appears between he and vav, toward the top-left of the vav. The candidate puts it on ה (יְהֹוָה). I treat this as an encoding-convention question and did not raise it as a discrepancy.
I did not re-examine a merkha under the pe of פֶּ֥ן beyond its general presence, because the final-nun descender sits right next to it. I saw no conflict.
